_about: Recorded accuracy anchors. This is the fixed point the accuracy gate
measures against, and it is the only accuracy reference that gates
anything in this harness.
Registered 2026-08-17. Andrew's ruling that day, in his words: the rule
for adopting a change 'should be about trading OUR accuracy for speed.
not tied to whatever lightgbm or catboost is fucking doing'. So an arm is
judged against ITS OWN recorded accuracy on the same scenario, at the same
tree count, on the same device. The peer comparison against CatBoost and
LightGBM continues on every run and gates nothing; it is a column.
WHY THIS IS A FILE AND NOT 'THE PREVIOUS RUN'. A reference that is
whatever ran last ratchets: lose 0.9 percent ten times, pass ten times,
end nine percent worse with every individual step defensible and the total
invisible. An absolute recorded value cannot do that. Drift accumulates
against a fixed point, which means it does not accumulate.
WHY IT IS SEPARATE FROM thresholds.json. That file holds policy: numbers
somebody chose, each carrying an argument. This file holds measurements:
numbers a run produced, each carrying provenance. The TOLERANCE lives in
thresholds.json under defaults.accuracy_anchor, where policy belongs.
HOW AN ENTRY GETS HERE, and there is no other way:
1. `python bench/real_data/verify.py <run> --propose-anchors <path>`
writes a candidate file. Nothing reads that file.
2. A person reads every entry, fills in `recorded_at`, `recorded_by` and
`why`, and moves it here.
3. The commit says what the anchor was adopted for.
No code path writes this file. `verify.py` only ever reads it. That is the
mechanism, not a convention: the deliberate half of the deliberate act is
done by a human, and the old and the new number appear together in a diff.
AN IMPROVEMENT DOES NOT MOVE AN ANCHOR EITHER. Same procedure, both
directions. `verify.check_differential` already treats a large unexplained
improvement as evidence that the two sides were not given the same
problem; auto-adopting one would auto-adopt exactly that class of fault.
AN EMPTY `anchors` OBJECT MEANS NOTHING IS COVERED. It does not mean
everything is fine. verify.py warns per arm-cell on a missing anchor, and
that warning is the accuracy gate reporting that it is not running.
Key format, built by verify._anchor_key:
scenario|tier|data_kind|dataset|arm|device|n<trees>
Threads are deliberately absent: our arms are reproducible across thread
counts and check_determinism gates it, so a metric that moves with the
thread count is a defect this gate should catch rather than a new cell it
should abstain on. The device IS present: the accelerator histogram
reduction is fixed point on purpose, so one anchor covering both backends
would let a real regression on one hide behind the other.
Only the PRIMARY metric gates. `quality` records the full metric set so
that a later decision to gate a secondary costs no re-run.
A STALE ANCHOR IS MARKED, NOT RECOMPUTED. Added 2026-08-17.
An anchor can stop describing the model we ship with no number in it
changing: our `lambda_l2` under non-symmetric growth policies moved from
0.0 to 1.0 that day, so any anchor recorded from an arm that left that key
UNSET was taken on a model we no longer ship. Recomputing such an anchor by
arithmetic would install exactly the ratchet this file exists to prevent, so
it is neither edited nor deleted. It stops gating, it WARNs on every run,
and a fresh run replaces it.
That is decided mechanically and not from a list somebody maintains. Each
entry carries a `configuration` block, written by
`verify.propose_anchors` from the record, holding what the fit resolved for
the tracked parameters and which of them the ARM LEFT UNSET.
`verify.anchor_staleness` compares the unset ones against what they resolve
to now, read from python/mojotrees/sklearn.py. So an anchor proposed AFTER a
default moves is current by construction, and the run is what clears the
staleness. `verify.STALE_ANCHOR_PARAMETERS` names the tracked parameters.
An entry with NO `configuration` block cannot be judged either way and is
reported as ANCHOR CURRENCY UNKNOWN, which also does not gate. That is the
same rule as a missing anchor and a missing cpu twin: a check that cannot
run says so rather than passing.
An entry may also carry an explicit `stale` block, `{since, why,
cleared_by}`, which is authoritative and wins over the comparison, for a
reason no comparison can see. Nothing in this harness writes it.
NOTHING IS STALE TODAY BECAUSE NOTHING IS ANCHORED. `anchors` is empty and
has been since the concept landed, so the 2026-08-17 `lambda_l2` move made
no entry here stale: there were none. docs/design/ACCURACY_BUDGET.md
section 13 says these anchors 'were measured at lambda_l2 = 0' and that is
true of the run artifacts under bench/results, not of this file. The
mechanism above is built for the anchors the pending run will produce, and
for the next time a default moves.

configuration.note: `passed` is what the harness handed the estimator, where None means UNSET. `followed_default` is that subset, and it is the only subset a package default change can invalidate. `shipped_at_record` is what the matching sklearn.py constant held when this run was taken, chosen per grow policy because symmetrictree resolves an unset key from CatBoost's constant and every other policy from LightGBM's. verify.anchor_staleness compares the two

recorded_from.recorded_by: Andrew Hendel, adopted by instruction in session cascadeprojects-49bb

dense_regression|standard|real|year_pred.why: Adopted 2026-08-17 as the FIRST anchors this repository has ever held. Until this commit `anchors` was empty, which meant the accuracy gate covered nothing and, worse, that `check_differential`'s deliberate narrowing to the mojotrees/cpu pair handed every variant arm and every GPU row to a gate that held nothing at all. Adopted from run 20260817T205811Z-e2e, which verifies 49 pass and 0 fail, and which is the first run taken after the prediction rewrite, so its numbers describe the code that ships rather than the code that preceded it. Adopted so that ACCURACY_BUDGET section 14's 0.25 percent per-scenario veto, and every pricing decision behind it including device-side MVS, has a fixed point to measure against. NOTE that every parameter in this arm's `configuration.passed` was named by the harness and none was left unset, so `followed_default` is empty and no package default change can make this entry stale. It goes stale only when the run is superseded deliberately.
